item: Tax on the ACT of converting your own CNY into USD
verified_rule_or_value: None of the nine closed categories of taxable personal income in IIT Law Art. 2 is 'currency conversion'. No instrument reviewed in this session imposes a tax on the act of exchange itself.
what_it_means: This is a statement that the reviewed instruments contain no such tax. It is NOT a ruling that no PRC tax can arise in connection with moving this money: tax depends on how the money was earned, on your residence status under Art. 1, and on whether earlier PRC tax was paid.

item: IIT on the income that CREATED the money
verified_rule_or_value: Comprehensive income (wages, labour remuneration, author's remuneration, royalties): excess-progressive 3%-45%. Business income: excess-progressive 5%-35%. Interest, dividends, bonuses, property leasing, PROPERTY TRANSFER and incidental income: proportional 20%.
what_it_means: The tax that actually bites is the tax on the underlying income, and it is due whether or not the money ever leaves China. The bank's demand for a tax certificate under Guidelines Art. 59 is evidence that this has been settled — it is not a new conversion levy.

item: Tax base on a property sale
verified_rule_or_value: Proceeds less the original value of the property and reasonable expenses, taxed at 20%.
what_it_means: Not 20% of the sale price. Art. 6(5) sets the base as the gain.

item: Pre-emigration tax clearance
verified_rule_or_value: Mandatory, and it must be completed BEFORE the household registration is cancelled.
what_it_means: Art. 10(5) makes cancelling a Chinese hukou because of emigrating abroad a filing trigger; Art. 13 para 4 requires the tax clearance before the cancellation. Because 汇发〔2014〕2号 §6 routes the emigrant property transfer through the ORIGINAL hukou location, the clearance gates the whole route.

item: PRC foreign tax credit for a resident individual
verified_rule_or_value: Foreign IIT already paid may be credited against the PRC tax due on that foreign income, capped at the PRC tax computed on the same income under the IIT Law.
what_it_means: Applies to a PRC RESIDENT individual's foreign-source income — the mirror image of the U.S. credit, and relevant only if you also have foreign income reportable in China.

item: Currency used for PRC tax computation
verified_rule_or_value: Income in a currency other than RMB is converted at the RMB exchange-rate MIDPOINT.
what_it_means: Note the contrast with the cost model: the tax authority uses the midpoint, while a customer purchasing USD pays the bank's ask. The two are different rates for different purposes and must not be mixed.

item: Federal income tax on the currency movement itself
verified_rule_or_value: §988(e)(1): the rest of §988 does not apply to a section 988 transaction entered into by an individual which is a PERSONAL transaction. §988(e)(2): on a personal disposition of nonfunctional currency, no gain is recognised by reason of post-acquisition exchange-rate changes — but that sentence does NOT apply if the gain that would otherwise be recognised EXCEEDS USD 200.
what_it_means: Three things must be true for the exclusion to hold, and none is determinable from the material reviewed: the disposition must be of NONFUNCTIONAL currency (§988(c)(1)(C)(ii) expressly includes bank deposits, so a CNY deposit qualifies for a USD-functional taxpayer); the transaction must be PERSONAL; and the gain must not exceed USD 200. §988(e)(3) withdraws 'personal' status to the extent allocable expenses meet §162 (other than §162(a)(2) travel) or §212 (other than the tax-related part).

item: Character and source of any §988 gain that IS taxable
verified_rule_or_value: Ordinary income or loss, computed separately. For an individual the source follows the country of the tax home under §911(d)(3); with no tax home, a U.S. citizen is resident in the United States.
what_it_means: If the exclusion does not hold, the gain is ordinary, not capital, and is U.S.-source for a U.S.-tax-home citizen — which matters because a foreign tax credit is generally not available against U.S.-source income.

item: TY2026 foreign earned income exclusion
verified_rule_or_value: USD 132,900 for tax year 2026, up from USD 130,000 for 2025.
what_it_means: An exclusion for qualifying FOREIGN EARNED INCOME. It is not a mechanism for repatriating an existing bank balance and it does not apply to investment income, gains, or the conversion itself.

item: CY2026 annual gift exclusion
verified_rule_or_value: USD 19,000 per donee for calendar year 2026, unchanged from 2025. The exclusion for gifts to a spouse who is NOT a U.S. citizen rises to USD 194,000 for calendar year 2026, from USD 190,000.
what_it_means: Relevant only if part of the balance is being given rather than moved. The non-citizen-spouse figure is the one most often missed and it is materially larger.

item: FBAR filing obligation
verified_rule_or_value: A U.S. person must file FinCEN Form 114 where the AGGREGATE value of foreign financial accounts EXCEEDED USD 10,000 at ANY TIME during the calendar year. Due 15 April with an automatic extension to 15 October; filed electronically via the BSA E-Filing System, not with the return; records kept five years.
what_it_means: The test is aggregate across all accounts and is 'exceeded', not 'reached'. A single Chinese account holding USD 10,001 at any point in the year triggers it. This obligation exists independently of whether any money moves.

item: FBAR penalty — non-willful
verified_rule_or_value: Statutory maximum USD 10,000; inflation-adjusted maximum USD 16,536 for penalties assessed on or after 17 January 2025. A REASONABLE CAUSE EXCEPTION applies: no penalty where the violation was due to reasonable cause AND the amount or balance was properly reported.
what_it_means: The reasonable-cause exception is statutory, at §5321(a)(5)(B)(ii). It is unavailable for a willful violation.

item: FBAR penalty — willful
verified_rule_or_value: The GREATER OF USD 100,000 statutory (inflation-adjusted to USD 165,353) OR 50 PERCENT OF the amount determined under §5321(a)(5)(D) — for a failure to report the existence of an account, THE BALANCE IN THE ACCOUNT AT THE TIME OF THE VIOLATION. The reasonable-cause exception does not apply.
what_it_means: On a USD 400,000 balance, 50% is USD 200,000, which exceeds the USD 165,353 adjusted fixed maximum, so the 50% limb governs. This is the single largest number in the whole analysis and it is a REPORTING penalty, not a tax and not an exchange cost.

item: FBAR penalty — the adjusted maxima are not a total cap
verified_rule_or_value: 31 CFR 1010.821(b): the adjusted maximum amounts do NOT limit the total penalty where a penalty may be imposed for each day a violation continues.
what_it_means: Multiple years and continuing violations stack. The figures in T12 and T13 are per-violation maxima, not a ceiling on total exposure.

item: Structuring penalty
verified_rule_or_value: For a violation of 31 U.S.C. §5324, a civil money penalty of up to the FULL AMOUNT of the currency involved in the transaction.
what_it_means: The U.S. counterpart to the PRC anti-splitting rule, and it is harsher in form: up to 100% of the amount structured, not a percentage band.

item: Assessment window, cumulation and repeat-violator uplift
verified_rule_or_value: Six years from the date of the transaction to assess (§5321(b)(1)). A civil penalty may be imposed even where a criminal penalty is imposed for the same violation (§5321(d)). For a repeat violator, an ADDITIONAL civil penalty of up to the greater of three times the profit gained or loss avoided, or twice the maximum penalty (§5321(f)).
what_it_means: The §5321(f) uplift counts only previous violations occurring after the enactment date of the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 (1 January 2021).

item: PRC penalty — unlawful outward transfer (逃汇)
verified_rule_or_value: Order to repatriate within a time limit, plus a fine of UP TO 30% of the amount evaded; where the circumstances are serious, BETWEEN 30% AND THE EQUIVALENT AMOUNT (i.e. up to 100%); criminal liability where a crime is constituted.
what_it_means: 30% is a CEILING for an ordinary case, not a floor. The 30%-100% band applies only 情节严重 (where the circumstances are serious).

item: PRC penalty — private or disguised FX dealing (地下钱庄)
verified_rule_or_value: Warning, confiscation of illegal gains, plus a fine of UP TO 30% of the illegal amount; where serious, BETWEEN 30% AND THE EQUIVALENT AMOUNT; criminal liability where a crime is constituted.
what_it_means: Reaches 私自买卖外汇, 变相买卖外汇 (disguised dealing, which is how informal value transfer and token-based moves are characterised), 倒买倒卖 and illegal brokering in a relatively large amount.

item: PRC penalty — illegal FX arbitrage with false documents (非法套汇)
verified_rule_or_value: Order to convert the illegally arbitrated funds back, plus a fine of UP TO 30% of that amount; where serious, BETWEEN 30% AND THE EQUIVALENT AMOUNT; criminal liability where a crime is constituted.
what_it_means: This is the article that reaches a purchase made on fabricated invoices or false transaction documents.

item: PRC penalty — carrying FX across the border unlawfully
verified_rule_or_value: Warning, plus a fine of UP TO 20% of the illegal amount. Where laws or administrative regulations provide for Customs to impose the penalty, those provisions prevail.
what_it_means: A lower band than Arts. 39/40/45, but still material, and Customs may be the enforcing authority.

item: PRC penalty — documentary and registration failures by an individual
verified_rule_or_value: Order to correct plus a warning, and a fine of UP TO RMB 50,000 for an individual (up to RMB 300,000 for an institution).
what_it_means: Covers failure to make the balance-of-payments declaration, failure to submit valid documents or submitting untrue documents, FX account and FX registration violations, and obstructing a SAFE inspection.
